basis: Infection directly inflames the meninges of the brain or spinal cord.
Malignant neoplasm located in the dermis.
Mature teratoma arising in the central nervous system.
Infiltrative vascular tumor commonly involving skin; platelet trapping, hemolysis and consumptive coagulopathy occur in 30-79%.
Aspergillus infection or hypersensitivity predominantly affects lungs; extrapulmonary damage is uncommon. Neutropenia is usually a predisposing condition.
Blistering, hair/nail disease and intellectual disability define syndrome; corneal opacity occurs in 30-79%. Pneumonia is a separate infection.
Malignant hypertension with hypertensive renal injury defines the concept.
Most benign fibrous histiocytomas are cutaneous dermatofibromas; deep soft-tissue forms are uncommon.
Defined by congenital abnormalities of the cornea, pupil and macula.
Autoimmune skin and muscle inflammation; vasculitis occurs in 30-79%. Restrictive ventilation can reflect muscle weakness; pulmonary fibrosis is 5-29%.
Thiamine transport disorder with severe brain maldevelopment; osteoporosis 30-79%; optic atrophy and foveal hypoplasia reported in 1/1, with limited ocular evidence.
Inherited cortical myoclonus, tremor and epilepsy; occasional transient visual symptoms do not establish ocular damage.
Named inherited hyaluronan metabolic defect; definition and organ phenotype evidence are absent, preventing additional organ assignment.
Umbrella disorder of peripheral arteries and veins; no additional organ injury is common across its subtypes.
Inherited mitochondrial iron-sulfur metabolism defect causing sideroblastic anemia; hepatic iron deposition alone is insufficient, and cirrhosis is 5-29%.
Melanoma arising in the anus; gastrointestinal site determines the organ label.
Benign tumor arising in sebaceous glands of the skin.
Lysosomal disorder defined by myoclonus, ataxia and progressive visual loss; hearing loss 80-99% per HPO. Reported skeletal/skin findings omitted at cap.
Carcinoma originating in breast lobules; breast has no axis. Metastatic sites are not defining organ involvement.
Severe infantile hepatocardiomuscular fatty-acid oxidation disorder; liver and heart disease characterize this form; myopathy occurs in 30-79%.
Defined as a disorder of skeletal joints; immune mechanisms do not apply to every subtype.
Genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with seizures, profound developmental impairment and brain atrophy.
Arterial dissection, medial necrosis and lentigines define syndrome. Hemiparesis occurs in 30-79%, but persistent direct CNS injury is not established.
Alobar forebrain malformation; hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction, particularly diabetes insipidus, affects roughly 50-70% of HPE. Craniofacial defects vary.
Carcinoma arising in a salivary-gland pleomorphic adenoma, usually in the parotid; salivary glands belong to gastrointestinal.
